purpose: Authoritative registry of all agents in the delivery system. Defines agent roles, handoff contracts, execution order, folder ownership, entry and exit criteria, and cross-agent coordination rules. All agents operate on approved documents and communicate exclusively through meta.json sidecars.
core_principle: Agents coordinate through approved documents, explicit status transitions, and typed handoff contracts. No agent may act on unapproved inputs. No agent may produce outputs outside its assigned folder. The runner enforces all approval gates.

agent_registry.name: Reviewer
agent_registry.primary_input: task, plan, implementation, evidence (varies by review target)

agent_registry.name: Memory Manager
agent_registry.primary_input: approved plans, tasks, reviews, implementation outcomes

workflow_order: 4. Task Decomposer: build task graph (02b_task_graph) and task contracts (03_task)
5. Reviewer: review task graph (04_review → task graph approved)
6. Implementation Planner: define implementation plan per task (04_implementation_plan)
8. Executor: implement code and tests per approved plan
11. Memory Manager: preserve durable project knowledge (06_memory)

handoff_contracts.rule: Planner must not start until initiative status is approved. Initiative ID must be preserved in plan linkage.
Task Decomposer must not start until plan status is approved. Task IDs must derive from plan task breakdown table verbatim.
Reviewer assesses graph completeness, linkage integrity, and coverage against the approved plan. Decision must be explicit: approved or rejected.
Implementation Planner must not start until task status is approved. File plan is mandatory. Scope must not expand beyond the task contract.
Executor must not start until implementation plan is approved. Executor must not deviate from the file plan or add unsolicited scope.
Reviewer performs independent assessment against the implementation plan. Validation is a separate artifact from review. Both must be produced with explicit decisions.

handoff_contracts.input: approved plans, tasks, reviews, implementation outcomes
handoff_contracts.rule: Memory Manager only records stable, approved knowledge. Transient state, rejected artifacts, and speculative knowledge must not be persisted.

cross_agent_rules.role_isolation: Each agent performs only its designated role. Planners do not decompose tasks. Executors do not review. Reviewers do not implement.
cross_agent_rules.document_first: Agents act on documents, not on conversations or implicit agreements. Every decision is recorded in an artifact.
cross_agent_rules.no_scope_drift: Agents must not expand scope beyond what is defined in their input contract. Scope changes require a new initiative or plan amendment.
cross_agent_rules.explicit_decisions: Every agent output must include an explicit status (approved/rejected/drafted). Ambiguous outputs are rejected by the runner.
cross_agent_rules.canonical_linking: Every artifact must reference its parent artifact by ID. Orphaned artifacts are invalid.
cross_agent_rules.deterministic_naming: Artifact filenames follow the convention defined in the template registry. Non-conforming filenames are rejected.
cross_agent_rules.approved_inputs_only: An agent must not begin work if its required input artifact does not have an approved status.
cross_agent_rules.rejected_means_stop: A rejected sidecar halts the current workflow step. The runner routes to the appropriate upstream state per the rejection routing table.
cross_agent_rules.superseded_means_inactive: Superseded artifacts are immutable and inactive. Agents must not act on superseded inputs.
cross_agent_rules.traceability_is_mandatory: Every artifact must be traceable to its originating initiative via an unbroken chain of document linkage.

validation_model: Validation is performed by the Reviewer agent independently from the Executor. No agent validates its own output. The meta.json sidecar is the only communication channel between agents and the runner.
future_automation_notes: This registry is designed for future control plane automation. Agent IDs are stable references for workflow configuration. Handoff contracts are typed and machine-readable. Entry and exit criteria are enumerable and can be checked programmatically. The runner currently enforces approval gates; a future control plane can enforce all criteria automatically.
